summary: Cross-tenant SIEM export: duplicate events and timestamp offset normalization for multi-region webhook replay
description: Customer reports duplicated audit events and inconsistent timestamps after enabling the cross-region SIEM webhook bridge. Events appear twice when our retry/resend path overlaps with a replay from the customer side. Timestamps from eu-west region appear in their Splunk index with +1s offsets and inconsistent timezone fields, causing rule mismatches and billing attribution problems.
impact: Splunk correlation rules and alerting for Acme (enterprise) are firing twice for the same user actions during heavy ingestion windows. Customer is seeing inflated compliance event counts for end-of-day reporting and disputes with their SOC team. Business impact: elevated alert noise and potential audit disagreement with regulators.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer enables cross-region SIEM bridge for eu-west and us-east on their account.
2) Trigger a batch of ~5k activity events across two tenants in quick succession (test harness attached).
3) Simulate partial webhook ACK loss from Splunk (drop ACKs for a subset of events for 30s) to force retry/resend path.
4) Observe duplicated events in customer's Splunk index and mismatched _time values (some events shifted by +1s or with UTC offset tags missing).
5) Confirm duplicate canonical_event_id appears in our S3 raw delivery and again in the retry payload with different timestamp metadata.

Hypothesis: webhook dispatcher does not dedupe on canonical_event_id across resend window; timestamp normalization is applied per-delivery rather than per-event.

investigation_notes: Duplicate path identified: initial delivery + retry/resend overlap when Splunk ACK delayed > dispatcher.retry_window (defaults to 30s).

Timestamps: two normalization layers - (1) source event ts preserved in payload, (2) webhook-dispatcher applies 'delivered_at' which was being used by customer's ingestion mapping. Some deliveries used delivered_at, others used payload.ts leading to +1s discrepancies depending on timing of normalization code path.

Canonicalization: events include 'canonical_event_id' computed by audit-exporter as sha256(tenant|event_id|sequence). Retry uses same event_id but our dispatcher was re-computing event metadata and sometimes overwrote 'delivered_at' with current server time in milliseconds causing minor skew.
Observed customer Splunk mapping: their parsing rules favor header 'X-Redwood-Event-Time' if present else fall back to payload.ts. In retry path header was missing for a subset of deliveries.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided (2026-03-13 09:24): advise customer to enable HEC dedup by 'X-Redwood-Event-Id' and apply timestamp priority to canonical_event_ts header. Customer has toggled dedupe and confirmed reduced duplicates in a staged window.

Short-term server change (rolled as hotfix): webhook-dispatcher now preserves canonical_event_id and includes an explicit 'X-Redwood-Event-Id' and 'X-Redwood-Event-Time' headers on all delivery attempts (PR #7812). Hotfix deployed to prod-us-east and prod-eu-west at 2026-03-13 03:40 UTC.

Customer-facing corrected counts: created a one-off reconciliation export for Acme covering 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-13 (s3://redwood-exports/acme/2026-03-12/reconciled-counts.csv) and shared via secure SFTP.

Permanent fix pending: implement server-side idempotent delivery filter that will drop duplicate canonical_event_id within tenant-specific watermark window and canonicalize timestamp fields deterministically before delivery.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4041: Implement tenant-watermark idempotency filter in webhook-dispatcher (ensure low-latency memtable with eviction).
INT-4099: Expand audit-exporter test harness to include ACK-drop scenarios and timezone-normalization unit tests.
Create docs: 'SIEM onboarding: recommended HEC dedupe + headers' and add to customer onboarding checklist.
Ops: monitor post-hotfix for two additional days and run reconciliation job nightly for affected tenant until permanent fix rollout.
resolution: Workaround applied; hotfix deployed to preserve idempotency headers; reconciliation export delivered to customer. Permanent idempotency filter and timestamp canonicalization scheduled as internal tasks.
